segments.text: Good morning. Please sit down. What brings you in today?
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Doctor, I have been having a bad cough for about five days now. And since yesterday I have fever also.
segments.speaker: patient

segments.text: Any chest pain, or difficulty in breathing?
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: No chest pain. But I feel short of breath when I climb the stairs.
segments.speaker: patient

segments.text: Is the cough dry, or is there phlegm?
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: There is phlegm. Yellowish in color, mostly in the morning.
segments.speaker: patient

segments.text: Any history of asthma?
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Do you smoke?
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: No asthma.
segments.speaker: patient

segments.text: I used to smoke, but I stopped four years back.
segments.speaker: patient

segments.text: Let me check your vitals.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Your temperature is 101.2 Fahrenheit.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Blood pressure is 130 over 85.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Pulse is 96.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Oxygen saturation is 97% on Ruhmair.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Now let me listen to your chest.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Take a deep breath.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: I can hear some crackles in the right lower zone.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: This looks like a lower respiratory tract infection, most likely bacterial.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: I do not think it is pneumonia, but I want a chest X-ray to be sure.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Is it serious, doctor?
segments.speaker: patient

segments.text: It is treatable.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: I am starting you on a moxicillin, 500 milligrams, three times a day, after food, for five days.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Please complete the full course even if you feel better.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: For the fever, take paracetamol 650 milligrams, only when needed, up to three times a day.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Do not take more than that.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Should I take any cough syrup?
segments.speaker: patient

segments.text: Yes.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Two teaspoons at bedtime, for five days.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: It may make you drowsy, so do not drive after taking it.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Drink plenty of warm fluids and take rest.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: If the fever does not come down in three days, or if you get breathing difficulty, come back
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: immediately.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Otherwise, come for a follow-up after one week, with the X-ray report.
segments.speaker: doctor

segments.text: Thank you doctor.
segments.speaker: patient
